1: # v8r
2: 
3: ![Build status](https://github.com/chris48s/v8r/workflows/Run%20tests/badge.svg?branch=main)
4: [![codecov](https://codecov.io/gh/chris48s/v8r/branch/main/graph/badge.svg?token=KL998A5CJH)](https://codecov.io/gh/chris48s/v8r)
5: ![NPM version](https://img.shields.io/npm/v/v8r.svg)
6: ![License](https://img.shields.io/npm/l/v8r.svg)
7: ![Node Compatibility](https://img.shields.io/node/v/v8r.svg)
8: 
9: A command-line JSON and YAML validator that's on your wavelength.
10: 
11: ## Getting Started
12: 
13: One-off:
14: ```bash
15: npx v8r <filename>
16: ```
17: 
18: Local install:
19: ```bash
20: npm install -g v8r
21: v8r <filename>
22: ```
23: 
24: ## Usage Examples
25: 
26: ```bash
27: # v8r queries https://www.schemastore.org/ to detect a suitable schema based on the filename
28: $ v8r package.json  # v8r can validate JSON..
29: Validating package.json against schema from https://json.schemastore.org/package ...
30: 
31: Errors:
32: [
33:   {
34:     keyword: 'type',
35:     dataPath: '.name',
36:     schemaPath: '#/properties/name/type',
37:     params: { type: 'string' },
38:     message: 'should be string'
39:   }
40: ]
41: 
42: ❌ package.json is invalid
43: 
44: $ v8r action.yml  # ..and YAML
45: Validating action.yml against schema from https://json.schemastore.org/github-action ...
46: ✅ action.yml is valid
47: 
48: 
49: # if v8r can't auto-detect a schema for your file..
50: $ v8r feature.geojson
51: ❌ Could not find a schema to validate feature.geojson
52: 
53: # ..you can specify one
54: $ v8r feature.geojson -s https://json.schemastore.org/geojson
55: Validating feature.geojson against schema from https://json.schemastore.org/geojson ...
56: ✅ feature.geojson is valid
57: ```
58: 
59: ## Exit codes
60: 
61: * v8r always exits with code `0` when:
62:     * The input file was validated against a schema and the input file was **valid**
63:     * `v8r` was called with `--help` or `--version` flags
64: 
65: * By default v8r exits with code `1` when an error was encountered trying to validate the input file. For example:
66:     * No suitable schema could be found
67:     * An error was encountered during an HTTP request
68:     * The input file did not exist
69:     * The input file was not JSON or yaml
70:     * etc
71: 
72:     This behaviour can be modified using the `--ignore-errors` flag. When invoked with `--ignore-errors` v8r will exit with code `0` even if one of these errors was encountered while attempting validation. A non-zero exit code will only be issued if validation could be completed successfully and the file was invalid.
73: 
74: * v8r always exits with code `99` when:
75:     * The input file was validated against a schema and the input file was **invalid**
76: 
77: ## FAQ
78: 
79: ### ❓ How does `v8r` decide what schema to validate against if I don't supply one?
80: 
81: 💡 `v8r` queries the [Schema Store catalog](https://www.schemastore.org/) to try and find a suitable schema based on the name of the input file.
82: 
83: ### ❓ My file is valid, but it doesn't validate against one of the suggested schemas.
84: 
85: 💡 `v8r` is a fairly thin layer of glue between [Schema Store](https://www.schemastore.org/) (where the schemas come from) and [ajv](https://www.npmjs.com/package/ajv) (the validation engine). It is likely that this kind of problem is either an issue with the schema or validation engine.
86: 
87: * Schema store issue tracker: https://github.com/SchemaStore/schemastore/issues
88: * Ajv issue tracker: https://github.com/ajv-validator/ajv/issues
89: 
90: ### ❓ What JSON schema versions are supported?
91: 
92: 💡 `v8r` works with JSON schema draft-04, draft-06 and draft-07.
93: 
94: ### ❓ Will 100% of the schemas on schemastore.org work with this tool?
95: 
96: 💡 No. There are some with [known issues](https://github.com/chris48s/v8r/issues/18)
97: 
98: ### ❓ Can `v8r` validate against a local schema?
99: 
100: 💡 Nope. There are other better tools for this. If you want to validate against a local schema, I recommend [ajv-cli](https://github.com/ajv-validator/ajv-cli/).

4: const callCounter = {};

7: function expire(cache, ttl) {
8:   Object.entries(cache.all()).forEach(function ([url, cachedResponse]) {
9:     if (!("timestamp" in cachedResponse) || !("body" in cachedResponse)) {
10:       console.debug(`ℹ️ Cache error: deleting malformed response`);
11:       cache.removeKey(url);
12:     } else if (Date.now() > cachedResponse.timestamp + ttl) {
13:       console.debug(`ℹ️ Cache stale: deleting cached response from ${url}`);
14:       cache.removeKey(url);
15:     }
16:     cache.save(true);
17:   });
18: }

20: function limitDepth(url) {
21:   /*
22:   It is possible to create cyclic dependencies with external references
23:   in JSON schema. Ajv doesn't detect this when resolving external references,
24:   so we keep a count of how many times we've called the same URL.
25:   If we are calling the same URL over and over we've probably hit a circular
26:   external reference and we need to break the loop.
27:   */
28:   if (url in callCounter) {
29:     callCounter[url]++;
30:   } else {
31:     callCounter[url] = 1;
32:   }
33:   if (callCounter[url] > callLimit) {
34:     throw new Error(
35:       `❌ Called ${url} ${callLimit} times. Possible circular reference.`
36:     );
37:   }
38: }
39: 
40: async function cachedFetch(url, cache, ttl) {
41:   limitDepth(url);
42:   expire(cache, ttl);
43:   const cachedResponse = cache.getKey(url);
44:   if (cachedResponse !== undefined) {
45:     console.debug(`ℹ️ Cache hit: using cached response from ${url}`);
46:     return cachedResponse.body;

48:

51:     const resp = await got(url);
52:     const parsedBody = JSON.parse(resp.body);
53:     if (ttl > 0) {
54:       cache.setKey(url, { timestamp: Date.now(), body: parsedBody });
55:       cache.save(true);
56:     }
57:     return parsedBody;
58:   } catch (error) {
59:     if (error.response) {
60:       throw new Error(`❌ Failed fetching ${url}\n${error.response.body}`);
61:     }
